messages:
alex: quick Q — noticed tenant alerts oscillating after we enabled quota-based gating. SLO thresholds in console are the same, but notify routing keeps flipping tiers. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

 tara: yup saw it on staging. looks like our notify policy uses per-tenant error rate + burst smoothing, but gating kicks in when quota burn spike happens, causing reroute to fallback channel. leads to duplicate tickets.

 ben: can you paste an example signal + routing config? I suspect noisy sampling window is too short.

 alex: here's the policy we're shipping:
```yaml
notify:
  primary: team-alerts
  fallback: infra-oncall
  gate:
    type: quota
    threshold: 0.8
    window_sec: 60
slo:
  target: 99.9
  alert_after: 5m
```

 maria: two issues: 1) gate.window_sec=60 is tiny for our telemetry smoothing, 2) alert_after=5m vs quota window mismatch.

 ben: agree — we should decouple gating signal from immediate notify routing. propose: add 'cooldown' and 'sampled_quorum' fields so occasional quota spikes don't flip routing.

 sre-oncall: from an ops POV, we want early visibility for true SLA-breaches but not for short-lived quota bursts. Maybe a tiered gating policy: only escalate to infra-oncall if gate persists for N windows OR if error budget burn rate > X.

 tara: +1. UX request: console should surface both 'routing rationale' and 'recent gate history' on the alert card so product teams can see why fallback happened.

 alex: new plan: change window_sec -> 300, add cooldown 10m, and implement 'persistence_required: 2' (must hit gate twice). Ben can prototype API change; Tara can mock console copy. Anyone object?

 ben: fine, I'll open a small API PR and include a migration note.

 maria: also add telemetry counters: gate_evaluations, gate_transitions, routing_decisions for 90d. useful for tuning.

 deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-config-service v2.3.1 -> canary -> us-west-2 (job 8765)

 alex: thanks — will follow canary and file a short playbook update.
